**Findings**

1. High: [cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/remote/git.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/remote/git.go:52) makes `remote.Fetch` add `--unshallow` for every shallow repo, and [cmd/entire/cli/git_operations.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments/cmd/entire/cli/git_operations.go:352) uses that helper for ordinary branch fetches in `FetchAndCheckoutRemoteBranch`. That means a user running resume/checkout flows from a shallow clone will now silently convert their working clone into a full-history fetch, even though the shallow-history problem this PR is addressing is specific to checkpoint metadata ancestry. This should be scoped to the metadata/v2 repair paths, not baked into the generic fetch helper.

2. Medium: [cmd/entire/cli/git_operations.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments/cmd/entire/cli/git_operations.go:407) and [cmd/entire/cli/git_operations.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments/cmd/entire/cli/git_operations.go:459) removed the depth-limited behavior from `FetchMetadataTreeOnly` / `FetchV2MainTreeOnly`, but [cmd/entire/cli/resume.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments/cmd/entire/cli/resume.go:459) still treats that first fetch as the cheap path. It is no longer “tree-only” in the old sense; it now downloads the full commit history of the metadata ref minus blobs. On long-lived checkpoint branches, every first `resume`/`explain` lookup now pays that full-history network cost, which is a real regression from the prior tip-only probe.

Assumption: I reviewed `pr/1024` against `origin/main`.

Testing: I tried targeted `go test` runs for the touched packages, but in this environment `go test` failed before execution because module resolution is currently incomplete (`golang.org/x/*` and `github.com/betterleaks/betterleaks/detect` were reported missing).
I’m re-running the review from the current branch state and focusing on whether the earlier concerns still hold after the latest changes.

The branch changed materially since the last pass: shallow handling is now opt-in, so I’m checking whether that actually removes the user-facing regression and whether any new edge cases were introduced.
I’m checking a couple of edge paths now: checkpoint-remote fetches and the push/reconcile flow, since that’s where the new `Unshallow` option matters most.
I’m validating the updated branch with targeted tests where possible. If the environment still blocks module resolution, I’ll call that out and base the review strictly on code paths.

I found one area that could still be risky if it’s new in this branch: whether resume now fetches before consulting local metadata in a way that can overwrite a diverged local metadata ref. I’m checking that against `origin/main` so I don’t report an old behavior as a new regression.

No findings in the current branch diff against `origin/main`.

The two issues from the previous pass appear addressed: shallow handling is now opt-in via `FetchOptions.Shallow` / `Unshallow`, so ordinary branch fetches no longer silently deepen user clones, and the metadata “tree-only” path is back to `--depth=1` instead of pulling full history.

Residual risk: I could not run the targeted Go tests in this environment because module resolution is incomplete here (`golang.org/x/*` and `github.com/betterleaks/betterleaks/detect` were reported missing), so this is a static review only.
